plainTranslation: Opposite tastes and values that attract. You're drawn to what you don't share. Failure mode: friction over whose way is right. Treat the difference as range, not a referendum.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryDeep: What you each find lovely doesn't quite match. You love differently, and it can feel like a mismatch. Learn their love language instead of insisting on yours.
tension: The harder part is the moment the difference stops feeling interesting and starts feeling like a verdict. What feels generous to you can look reckless to them. What feels responsible to them can feel joyless to you. Nobody says it directly. It comes out as a small face at the restaurant bill, a certain silence about the purchase, a sense that the other person is quietly grading how you live. Few things sting like feeling judged for what genuinely makes you happy.
advice: This one needs you to say it out loud instead of letting it curdle. Tell them what the thing actually gives you. Ask them the same, and listen past the part you find baffling. You do not have to want the same life. You have to stop treating your own preferences as the obviously correct ones.
summaryShort: What you each find lovely doesn't quite match.
